description: Bug #1 — Jira fetch must capture EVERY issue under 'Issues in epic' for a feature regardless of the parent's own issue type or the child's project, and force a one-time re-sync of already-cached features so stale rows (e.g. MWTGPROV-4575 with only two MWTGNBOP subtasks and empty links) re-fetch to include NSLNM-784. Root cause: epic-children capture is gated on issue_type == 'epic' in BOTH fetchers (shared/rest_clients/jira_rest_client.py::fetch_issue line 416, and modules/jira_fetcher.py::fetch_jira_issue). Epic children are appended into issue.subtasks and persist via subtasks_json, so no cache-schema column is required; a cache marker bump invalidates pre-fix rows. This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002 (it supplies the full related-key set).
steps: In C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\shared\rest_clients\jira_rest_client.py, in JiraRestClient.fetch_issue (def line 288), change the epic-children gate at line 416 ('if issue.issue_type and issue.issue_type.lower() == "epic":') so the '"Epic Link" = "<key>"' search (line 418) ALWAYS runs for every parent. Before appending each child (near line 439), skip any key already present in issue.subtasks or issue.linked_issues (whole-key equality) to avoid duplicates. Raise maxResults from 20 to 50; keep the fields list unchanged.

In C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\TestSuiteGenerator\.worktrees\qmetry-multi-link\modules\jira_fetcher.py, apply the identical change in fetch_jira_issue: the 'if issue.issue_type and issue.issue_type.lower() == "epic":' epic-children block must always run, with the same by-key de-dup against issue.subtasks and issue.linked_issues and maxResults=50, so the browser fallback path matches the REST path.

In C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\TestSuiteGenerator\.worktrees\qmetry-multi-link\modules\database.py, invalidate pre-fix jira_cache rows so already-cached features re-fetch: make is_jira_stale (~line 445) return True for rows that predate this fix. Prefer a minimal approach: bump a schema/version marker consulted by is_jira_stale, or add a nullable schema_version column (DDL ~lines 95-107, written in save_jira ~line 409) and treat NULL/old as stale. Keep save_jira writing links_json from linked_issues and subtasks_json from subtasks (epic children ride in subtasks).

Add a hermetic test file tests/test_jira_epic_children_capture.py that monkeypatches JiraRestClient._get to return (a) a Feature-type parent issue with two real subtasks/links and (b) a /search result containing MWTGNBOP-5791, MWTGNBOP-5792, and NSLNM-784, and asserts all three epic-child keys land in issue.subtasks with no key dropped and no duplicate, even though issue_type is 'Feature'. Reuse the hermetic monkeypatch style from tests/test_qmetry_steps_source.py.

Record in findings how a manual cache refresh is triggered for a specific feature (e.g. delete that feature's jira_cache row, or rely on the now-stale path) so NSLNM-784 is re-fetched for MWTGPROV-4575.
acceptance_criteria: For a non-Epic parent (issue_type 'Feature'), both fetchers capture every 'Issues in epic' child across ANY project, de-duped by key, none dropped.
Already-cached features are treated as stale by is_jira_stale after the marker bump, forcing a re-fetch that includes NSLNM-784.
Captured epic children persist to subtasks_json and round-trip through load_jira into jira.subtasks.
tests/test_jira_epic_children_capture.py passes and the existing fast suite shows no new failures.
verification: C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_jira_epic_children_capture.py -q  (run from the worktree root) — passes
C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q -m "not slow"  (from the worktree root) — all pass, no new failures
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. (1) shared/rest_clients/jira_rest_client.py::fetch_issue — epic-children '"Epic Link" = "<key>"' search now ALWAYS runs for every parent (gate removed), maxResults 20->50, each child skipped if its key already appears in issue.subtasks OR issue.linked_issues (so a child that is also a link is captured once, not duplicated). (2) modules/jira_fetcher.py::fetch_jira_issue — identical change on the browser-fallback path (gate replaced with 'if True', maxResults=50, same by-key de-dup). (3) modules/database.py — added JIRA_FETCH_SCHEMA_VERSION=2 marker; jira_cache DDL gained a nullable 'schema_version' column; migration v1 ('ALTER TABLE jira_cache ADD COLUMN schema_version INTEGER') backfills pre-existing DBs via the existing _run_migrations; save_jira writes JIRA_FETCH_SCHEMA_VERSION; is_jira_stale returns True when schema_version IS NULL or < JIRA_FETCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, so every pre-fix cached row is stale and re-fetches (picking up NSLNM-784 for MWTGPROV-4575). links_json/subtasks_json writing is unchanged; epic children still ride in subtasks. (4) Added tests/test_jira_epic_children_capture.py (hermetic, monkeypatches JiraRestClient._get; Feature-type parent + /search of MWTGNBOP-5791/-5792/NSLNM-784 with 5791 also a link) — passes.

CACHE REFRESH / HOW TO FORCE A RE-FETCH FOR A SPECIFIC FEATURE: No manual step is required in normal operation — the next fetch for any feature whose cached row predates this fix sees schema_version NULL (or <2) and is_jira_stale() returns True, so the pipeline re-fetches automatically (run init_db() once so migration v1 adds the column to an existing tsg_cache.db). To force an immediate re-fetch of ONE feature regardless of age, delete its row: DELETE FROM jira_cache WHERE feature_id='MWTGPROV-4575'; (SQLite, DB at <TSG root>/tsg_cache.db). After re-fetch, MWTGPROV-4575's subtasks_json will include NSLNM-784 plus the two MWTGNBOP subtasks. Bump JIRA_FETCH_SCHEMA_VERSION again in any future fetch-logic change to re-trigger a global re-sync.

PREREQ FOR FEAT-002: issue.subtasks now carries the full related-key set (real subtasks + every epic child across any project), round-tripping through subtasks_json -> load_jira -> jira.subtasks.

VERIFICATION: tests/test_jira_epic_children_capture.py passes. Fast suite (-m 'not slow'): 417 passed, 3 skipped. Pre-existing, NOT caused by this change (verified by re-running with my source edits git-stashed): 26 collection errors 'No module named shared' (the nested worktree breaks jira_fetcher's relative _SHARED_PATH = parent.parent.parent/'shared'; the new test works around it by inserting the canonical C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\shared on sys.path) and 2 cache-data failures (test_ac_gate::test_4349_role_list_survives, test_near_dup_pruning::test_4136_recovers_its_jira_and_subtask_coverage) due to empty subtasks in the worktree's tsg_cache.db.
